comments.author: PhilipDeegan
comments.body: changing the default causes some tests to fail during validation that L1 is not touching the border, although I think this is a bit odd given nesting buffer doesn't apply in the case of periodic borders

comments.author: nicolasaunai
comments.body:
changing to 1?
which tests fail?
are periodic borders considered level borders? I'd say they should not but is that related to llnl/SAMRAI#311 ?

comments.author: PhilipDeegan
comments.body:
this test fails as the largest patch size is equal to the L0 domain size
I don't think it's related to samrai issues, but in general I've seen L1 patches against the periodic border with nesting buffer 1

comments.author: nicolasaunai
comments.body: I do not get what that condition is for, do you remember? I think we should force default 1 as 0 leads to bugs

comments.author: PhilipDeegan
comments.body:
I think the condition was us being a bit overzealous and should likely be dropped and the default set to 1 yes
it's possible for other boundary conditions the check makes sense.
The issue really comes down to a test with "largest_patch_size" == domain_size

comments.author: nicolasaunai
comments.body: Was this test designed to reveal the periodic L1 issue on SAMRAI ? llnl/SAMRAI#311

comments.author: nicolasaunai
comments.body: we should probably even raise an error if the user attempts to have nesting buffer <1

comments.author: PhilipDeegan
comments.body:
Was this test designed to reveal the periodic L1 issue on SAMRAI ? llnl/SAMRAI#311
